The reminder now stays quiet for `git commit -m"add export handler"`. The fix is committed as `6b771fd` on `main`.

**Cause:** `src/staging.py` scanned every letter of any word starting with `-` for the stage-all flag. The shell split `git commit -m"add export handler"` into one word, `-madd export handler`. The `a` in the message looked like `-a`, so the check reported a stage-all. A standalone `-m "-a"` was misread the same way.

**Fix:** the scan now stops at the first short option that takes a value (`m`, `F`, `C`, `c`, `t` for commit), since the rest of that word is the value. It also skips the value word after a standalone one like `-m`.

**Tests:** I added regression tests to `tests/test_staging.py` for quoted messages, `-F`, `-mavoid`, `-m "-a"`, and cases where `-a` still counts (`-am`, `-qam`, and `-a` after the message). I confirmed the new cases failed before the change. All 8 tests pass with `python3 -m unittest`.

**Commit:** only `src/staging.py` and `tests/test_staging.py` went in. Your uncommitted README note and the untracked `notes/` folder are untouched.

I couldn't read `~/.claude/settings.json`, which the sandbox denied, so I didn't check whether a user-level hook also prints the reminder. The bug is in the reminder's own logic, so that check wouldn't change the fix.
